A RISC-V processor built from the ISA specification up, pipelined into five
stages, then pushed through synthesis on a **Sky130 130 nm** process and scored
on **CoreMark**. Unlike a classroom processor that only has to simulate
correctly, this one is graded on a figure of merit combining cycle count,
critical-path length, and silicon area — so every architectural decision has to
pay for the hardware it costs.

| Metric | Baseline | This design |
|:--|--:|--:|
| CoreMark score | 507 | **2,298** |
| Clock period (critical path) | — | **4.17 ns** |
| Improvement | — | **4.5×** |

## Pipeline

The core splits into the classic five stages, each in its own module:

| Stage | File | Work |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Fetch | `fetch.sv` | PC update, instruction memory read |
| Decode | `decode.sv` | Register read, immediate extension, control decode |
| Execute | `execute.sv` | ALU operation, branch resolution |
| Memory | `mem.sv` | Data memory access |
| Writeback | `writeback.sv` | Result select and register write |

Supporting those are an `alu`, a `regfile`, a `controller`, a `csr_unit` for
control and status registers, and a `hazard` unit — plus the usual small
building blocks (`adder`, `cmp`, `extend`, `flopr`, `mux2`).

## Hazards

Pipelining is only free until two instructions in flight need the same
register. Three mechanisms handle that:

**Forwarding.** The hazard unit drives two-bit `ForwardAE` / `ForwardBE`
selects, routing a result straight from the Memory or Writeback stage back into
Execute instead of waiting for it to land in the register file. Most
back-to-back dependencies then cost nothing.

**Load-use interlock.** Forwarding can't rescue a load, because the data isn't
back from memory yet when the next instruction needs it. That case is detected
explicitly:

```systemverilog
assign lwStall = (((Rs1D == RdE) || (Rs2D == RdE)) &&
                  ((ResultSrcE == 2'b01) || (ResultSrcE == 2'b10)));
assign StallF  = lwStall;
assign StallD  = lwStall;
assign FlushE  = lwStall | PCSrcE;
```

Fetch and Decode stall for one cycle while Execute is flushed to a bubble.

**Branch flush.** A taken branch resolves in Execute, by which point the wrong
instruction is already in Decode, so `PCSrcE` flushes it.

## Branch Prediction

A static **BTFNT** (backward-taken, forward-not-taken) predictor exploits the
fact that backward branches are usually loop edges and therefore usually taken,
while forward branches are usually the exit condition and usually aren't. It
costs essentially no area — just a check of the immediate's sign bit — which
matters when area is in the denominator of the score.

## Why the Scoring Changes the Design

The figure of merit is roughly

$$\text{score} \propto \frac{1}{(\text{cycles} \times \text{critical path})^3 \cdot \text{area}}$$

Cycle count and critical path are cubed; area is not. That weighting pushes hard
toward *speed* and makes a deep combinational path expensive in a way that pure
simulation never reveals. Reducing cycles by adding logic is only worth it while
that logic stays off the critical path — which is exactly the trade that
forwarding (cheap, on the path) and BTFNT (nearly free, off the path) are
resolving.
